extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, EPO applicants, patent examiners, and researchers interested in EPO Enlarged Board jurisprudence
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological list of decisions and opinions of the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the European Patent Office, each establishing or clarifying legal standards governing patentability, procedure, admissibility and interpretation of the European Patent Convention (EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject-matter (Article 52 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement applicable to European patent applications and patents: Patentable subject-matter (Article 52).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core statutory requirement; decisions in the Enlarged Board interpret the scope of what counts as patentable subject-matter under Article 52.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 54 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Novelty as required by Article 54 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions interpret what constitutes the 'state of the art' and when subject-matter is novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Article 56 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Inventive step under Article 56 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlarged Board case law clarifies how inventive step should be assessed in various contexts (e.g., effect evidence, simulation inventions, dosage regimes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (Article 57 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Industrial applicability under Article 57 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the set of substantive patentability criteria considered by the Boards and the Enlarged Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Article 82 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Unity of invention under Article 82 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law addresses the administrative function of unity and its applicability (e.g., relevance after amendment in opposition, a priori/a posteriori unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency / disclosure of the invention (Article 83 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Disclosure / sufficiency under Article 83 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enlarged Board decisions address sufficiency in contexts such as evidence of technical effect and whether post-filing evidence can be used to support inventive step if the original disclosure supports the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims (Article 84 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Claims and clarity under Article 84 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law covers when clarity may be examined in opposition (only to the extent an amendment introduces non-compliance) and issues of claim interpretation when assessing patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments / added matter (Article 123 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal requirement: Amendments and added subject-matter under Article 123 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions elaborate limits on allowable amendments, including rules on disclaimers and added matter when amending claims or the patent text.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substantive distinction between method and use claims; allowability of second medical indications (G 1/83 et al.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headnote: 'No substantive distinction between method claims and use claims, allowability of second medical indications' (G 1/83, G 5/83, G 6/83).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that second medical use claims are allowable under the EPC framework; published headnotes available in official languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-establishment of rights available to opponents in certain circumstances (G 1/86)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Article 122(1) EPC implies reestablishment is available only to applicants and proprietors, 'an opponent who files a notice of appeal within the two-month time limit ... but who fails to file a statement setting out the grounds ... may apply for reestablishment of rights in respect of that failure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that opponents can seek restitutio in integrum for procedural failures subject to Article 122(1) conditions where appeal notice timely but grounds late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of opposition in connection with part of business assets (G 4/88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition — transfer — part of the business assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses consequences when an opposition (or opponent status) is transferred as part of business asset transfer; factual and legal consequences examined in decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim novel by its purpose; novelty of second non-medical indication (G 2/88; G 6/88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 123(3) — change of category — use claim novel by its purpose; Novelty — second non-medical indication yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that purpose-limited use claims can be novel and that second (non-medical) indications may confer novelty; partially identical holdings across decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention irrelevant when patent amended in opposition (G 1/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of unity of invention (Article 82 EPC) is not applicable under Article 102(3) EPC when a European patent is amended during opposition proceedings; unity has no relevance when a patent is amended in opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats unity as an administrative examination-time requirement whose function is fulfilled during examination and not for amendment assessment in opposition-maintenance context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality requirement extends to first-instance employees taking part in decisions (G 5/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of impartiality applies in principle also to employees of the departments of the first instance of the EPO taking part in decision‑making activities affecting the rights of any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies standards for suspected partiality and who can be considered subject to impartiality requirements within EPO departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal by sole appellant terminates substantive appeal proceedings (G 7/91; G 8/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appeal is withdrawn by the sole appellant, appeal proceedings are terminated at least insofar as substantive issues are concerned (applies to ex parte and inter partes proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural effect of withdrawal by sole appellant on continuation of appeal and substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections under Rule 88 are strictly declaratory (G 3/89; G 11/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 123(2) — strictly declaratory nature of Rule 88 corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 88 corrections are to be viewed as strictly declaratory; decisions explain limits on what can be corrected without introducing added matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product composition is state of the art when product is publicly available and can be analysed and reproduced (G 1/92)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. The chemical composition of a product is state of the art when the product as such is available to the public and can be analysed and reproduced by the skilled person, irrespective of whether reasons can be identified for analysing the composition. 2. Same principle applies mutatis mutandis to any other product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when a product on the market constitutes prior art for novelty purposes: availability plus analysability/reproducibility by skilled person is key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination limited to extent of opposition; dependent claims may be examined if prima facie in doubt (G 9/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of an Opposition Division or a Board of Appeal to examine and decide on maintenance depends upon the extent to which the patent is opposed (Rule 55(c)/now Rule 76(2)(c)). Claims dependent on an independent claim falling in opposition may be examined if their validity is prima facie in doubt on available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an opponent deliberately limits the scope of opposition, other subject-matter is not strictly 'opposed' though Boards may examine dependent claims where prima facie doubts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Division not obliged to consider all grounds; fresh grounds in appeal limited (G 10/91)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Opposition Division or Board of Appeal is not obliged to consider all Article 100 EPC grounds beyond those covered by the notice of opposition; the division should examine only properly submitted and substantiated grounds per Article 99(1) with exception under Article 114(1); fresh grounds in appeal may be considered only with patentee approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets procedural limits on which grounds may be considered at first instance and on appeal; emphasizes proper submission and substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings — absent party — new facts/evidence (G 4/92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings — party absent — relation to introduction of new facts or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes procedural rules on what can be done and considered if a party is absent from oral proceedings and when new facts/evidence are introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition by proprietor not admissible (G 9/93)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Enlarged Board decided that an opposition to a European patent by its own proprietor is not admissible, overturning earlier decision G 1/84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Led to the later introduction of limitation and revocation proceedings under EPC 2000; clarifies who may validly file an opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement that usurped earlier application be pending for lawful applicant to file (G 3/92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlawful applicant: No requirement that the earlier (usurped) European patent application be pending before the EPO for the lawful applicant to be able to file a new application under Article 61(1) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies entitlement rules for filing where an earlier application was usurped; decision includes dissenting opinion on reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of reformatio in peius and extent of appeal decision (G 4/93; related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework of appeal — extent (decision) — reformatio in peius (with minority opinion in some cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes limits on worsening the legal position of an appellant through appeal decisions and clarifies the scope of decisions on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for deposits of biological material (G 2/93)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification on the time limit applicable for deposits of biological material relevant to priority/filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision specifies applicable timing rules for such deposits; relevant for sufficiency and support when biological material is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying person's submissions in oral proceedings require permission and oversight (G 4/95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by an accompanying person during oral proceedings cannot be made as a matter of right, but only with permission of and at the discretion of the EPO; submissions must be made under continuing responsibility and control of the professional representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies to oral submissions by qualified patent lawyers of non-contracting states; emphasizes representative responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on correction under Rule 89 decided by technical board (G 8/95)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from a decision of an Examining Division refusing a request under Rule 89 (now Rule 140) for correction of the decision to grant is to be decided by a technical board of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates competence for appeals relating to corrections of grant texts to technical boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of straw-man opposition (G 3/97; G 4/97)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is admissible to file an opposition on behalf of a third party (the 'principal') acting through a 'straw man'; the principal cannot be regarded as a party to proceedings. Exception for abuse of process where circumvention of law occurs — opposition may be rejected as inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines status of straw man opponents and when courts may reject such oppositions for abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: No internal remedy to review final Board of Appeal decisions (pre-EPC2000) (G 1/97)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to review a final decision of a Board of Appeal was not provided for in the EPC at that time. With EPC 2000 (effective later) petitions for review are possible under Article 112a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains historical absence of internal review and later procedural developments introducing petitions for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant-variety claims and Article 53(b) EPC exclusions (G 1/98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headnote: (I) A claim wherein specific plant varieties are not individually claimed is not excluded from patentability under Article 53(b) EPC even though it may embrace plant varieties. (II) When examining a process claim for production of a plant variety, Article 64(2) EPC is not to be taken into consideration. (III) Exception to patentability in Article 53(b) applies to plant varieties irrespective of production method; plant varieties containing genes introduced by recombinant technology are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies interplay between plant variety exclusions and claim scope; important for biotech patentability assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month period for non-prejudicial disclosures uses actual filing date (G 3/98)
rubrics_metrics.description: For calculation of the six-month period referred to in Article 55(1) EPC (non-prejudicial disclosures), the relevant date is the date of the actual filing of the European patent application; the date of priority is not to be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects whether certain public disclosures fall within the grace period; priority date not used for this particular calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation fee non-payment does not retroactively annul designation (G 4/98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Without prejudice to Article 67(4) EPC, designation of a Contracting State does not retroactively lose effect if the designation fee has not been paid on time. Deemed withdrawal of a designation takes effect upon expiry of the relevant time limits (not on expiry of any late-payment grace period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies timing-effect of late payments and deemed withdrawals for designated states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of undisclosed disclaimers (G 1/03 & G 2/03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment by introduction of a disclaimer may not be refused under Art. 123(2) EPC 1973 solely because neither the disclaimer nor the subject‑matter excluded by it have a basis in the application as filed; principles for undisclosed disclaimers established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives criteria and limits for introducing undisclosed disclaimers; later cases refine and set tests for such disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPS does not create priority rights from non-Paris Convention states (G 2/02)
rubrics_metrics.description: TRIPS does not entitle an applicant to claim priority from filing in a state which was not at the relevant dates a member of the Paris Convention (but was a WTO/TRIPS member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies interplay of international treaties regarding entitlement to priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic methods exclusion under Article 53(c) EPC — claim features determining exclusion (G 1/04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body are prohibited from patentability by Article 53(c) EPC if the subject‑matter includes: (i) diagnostic reasoning representing the deductive decision phase as a purely intellectual exercise, (ii) preceding constitutive steps for making the diagnosis, and (iii) specific interactions with the body among these preceding steps which are technical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains which claim features bring a claimed diagnostic method within statutory exclusion and which steps may be considered technical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentability of inventions involving destruction of human embryos (G 2/06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stem cells: non-patentability of inventions involving the use and destruction of human embryos (Rule 28(c) EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies bioethical exclusion in rule-based context; relevant for biotech subject-matter eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of divisional filings after refusal (G 1/09)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following refusal by an Examining Division, the application remains pending until expiry of the time limit for filing a notice of appeal, so a divisional application under Article 76 EPC may be filed even after refusal until expiry of the two-month notice of appeal time limit under Article 108 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for applicants considering filing divisionals after a refusal but before appeal deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisclosed disclaimer that removes an embodiment is not allowable unless remaining claim directly and unambiguously disclosed (G 2/10)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment introducing a disclaimer that disclaims subject‑matter that was (positively) disclosed as an embodiment in the application as filed is not allowable under Article 123(2) EPC 'if the subject‑matter remaining in the claim after the introduction of the disclaimer is not, explicitly or implicitly, directly and unambiguously disclosed to the skilled person using common general knowledge, in the application as filed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits disclaimers that remove disclosed embodiments; requires that the post-disclaimer claim be directly and unambiguously derivable from the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction requests under Rule 140 are inadmissible in certain contexts (G 1/10)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent proprietor's request under Rule 140 EPC for correction of the text of a patent is inadmissible, 'irrespective of whether the error was made (or introduced) by the applicant or by the Examining Division' and 'independently of when it is filed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets strict admissibility limits for post-grant text corrections by proprietors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence delimitation between Legal and Technical Boards (G 1/11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Technical Board of Appeal, rather than the Legal Board, is competent for an appeal against a decision of an Examining Division refusing a request for refund of a search fee under Rule 64(2) EPC, when the decision has not been taken together with a decision granting or refusing a European patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates competence for fee-refund disputes depending on the context of the underlying decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility issues: identity of appellant & alleged error/correction (G 1/12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility of the appeal; identity of the appellant; alleged error and correction thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses procedural requirements for admissible appeals including who must be the appellant and how alleged formal errors are treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of appeals where a company ceased and was restored (G 1/13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an opponent company ceased to exist before issuance of the Opposition Division decision, and then was restored with retroactive effect under national law after filing the appeal, questions arise about admissibility of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision provides guidance on how corporate existence/ restoration under national law affects appeal admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (Article 84) only examinable in opposition to the extent an amendment introduces non-compliance (G 3/14)
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering whether a patent as amended meets Article 84 EPC for the purposes of Article 101(3) EPC, the claims of the patent may be examined for compliance with Article 84 only when, and then only to the extent that, the amendment introduces non-compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits when clarity can be used as a ground to refuse maintenance of patent after amendment in opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product claims to plants or seeds allowable — conventional breeding patentability (G 2/12 & G 2/13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product claims directed to plants or plant material are allowable — 'plants or seeds obtained through a conventional breeding methods are patentable.' (Tomatoes II and Broccoli II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overturns earlier restrictive interpretations; relevant to plant-breeding inventions and Article 53(b) exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for requests to propose removal from office (Art. 23 referrals e.g., Art. 23 1/15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 12a(5) RPEBA requires that a request under Article 12a(1) RPEBA specify individual incidents and the evidence for them, and give reasons why they constitute a serious ground within the meaning of Article 23(1) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets particularity and evidentiary standards for disciplinary/removal proceedings against members of the Boards of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial priority entitlement for generic 'OR' claims (G 1/15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the EPC, entitlement to partial priority may not be refused for a claim encompassing alternative subject-matter by virtue of generic expressions or otherwise (generic 'OR'‑claim) provided that said alternative subject‑matter has been disclosed in the priority document directly, implicitly, unambiguously and in an enabling manner; no other substantive conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies entitlement to partial priority when a claim covers multiple alternatives and some alternatives have priority support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisclosed disclaimers: must fulfil G 1/03 criteria and not provide technical contribution (G 1/16)
rubrics_metrics.description: For considering whether a claim amended by an undisclosed disclaimer is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC, the disclaimer must fulfil one of the G 1/03 criteria. The disclaimer may not provide a technical contribution to the subject-matter disclosed in the application as filed and may not become relevant for inventive step or sufficiency; it may not remove more than necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further refines the permissible use of undisclosed disclaimers and their impact on substantive patentability questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal deemed not filed vs inadmissible; reimbursement of appeal fee in specific timing cases (G 1/18)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is deemed not to have been filed — and the appeal fee must be reimbursed — in cases involving particular combinations of late filing of notice of appeal and/or late payment of appeal fee (three specific timing cases summarized in the opinion). This applies similarly to the filing of oppositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the legal distinction and consequences between an inadmissible appeal and one deemed not filed, tied to precise compliance with Article 108 timelines and fee payment timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party under Article 115 has no right to oral hearing on re-entry request; no suspensive effect; venue for oral proceedings (G 2/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A third party under Article 115 EPC who has lodged an appeal against grant has no right to an oral hearing before a Board of Appeal about their request to order re-entry into examination to remedy unclear claims (Article 84). Furthermore, such an appeal has no suspensive effect. (2) Oral proceedings before Boards of Appeal may be held in Haar without infringing Articles 113(1) and 116(1) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies procedural rights of third parties and permissible venues for oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plants and animals exclusively obtained by essentially biological processes are not patentable (G 3/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: '[P]lants and animals exclusively obtained by essentially biological processes are not patentable.' Interpretation of Article 53(b) EPC and Rule 28(2) EPC; overturning earlier G 2/12 & G 2/13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that products obtained exclusively by essentially biological processes fall under exclusion; significant for plant/animal breeding patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of computer-implemented simulations (G 1/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on patentability of computer-implemented simulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses whether and under what circumstances computer simulations can contribute to a technical character for patentability purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis for refusing due to double patenting (G 4/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a legal basis in the EPC for refusing a European patent application on the ground of double patenting: a European patent application can be refused under Articles 97(2) and 125 EPC if it claims the same subject‑matter as a European patent granted to the same applicant and does not form part of the state of the art under Article 54(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirms EPO practice pre-referral and analyzes travaux préparatoires; leaves some subsidiary questions open (definition of 'same subject-matter', 'same applicant', application during opposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Videoconference oral proceedings compatible with Article 116 during general emergency (G 1/21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question referred: Is conducting oral proceedings as a videoconference compatible with the right to oral proceedings in Article 116(1) EPC if not all parties consent? Answer: During a general emergency impairing in-person attendance, videoconference oral proceedings are compatible even if not all parties consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an emergency exception allowing virtual oral proceedings without unanimous party consent, tied to general emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of post-filing non-public evidence to prove technical effect allowed if effect is derivable from original disclosure (G 2/21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of evidence not publicly available before the filing date, submitted by a patentee to prove a technical effect relied on to establish inventive step: allowed provided that 'the skilled person, having the common general knowledge in mind, and based on the application as originally filed, would derive said effect as being encompassed by the technical teaching and embodied by the same originally disclosed invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits use of post-filing evidence for inventive-step purposes only where the asserted effect was inherent/derivable from the original disclosure to the skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO competence to assess entitlement to claim priority; rebuttable presumption of 'same applicant' (G 1/22 & G 2/22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal priority ('same applicant'): The EPO is competent to assess whether a party is entitled to claim priority under Article 87(1) EPC. There is a rebuttable presumption under the autonomous law of the EPC that the applicant claiming priority is indeed entitled to claim priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates competence and evidentiary presumptions concerning priority entitlement and 'same applicant' issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are the starting point; description and drawings must always be consulted when assessing patentability (G 1/24, from 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The claims are the starting point and the basis for assessing the patentability of an invention under Articles 52 to 57 EPC. The description and drawings shall always be consulted to interpret the claims when assessing the patentability of an invention under Articles 52 to 57 EPC, and not only if the person skilled in the art finds a claim to be unclear or ambiguous when read in isolation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms interpretive principle that description/drawings are always part of claim interpretation for patentability assessment, not merely for resolving ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product on market may still be state of the art even if its internal composition could not be analysed before filing (G 1/23, from 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: State of the art character (Article 54(2) EPC) of a product when 'its composition or internal structure could not be analysed and reproduced without undue burden by the skilled person before [the filing date]': 'A product put on the market before the date of filing of a European patent application cannot be excluded from the state of the art within the meaning of Article 54(2) EPC for the sole reason that its composition or internal structure could not be analysed and reproduced by the skilled person before that date.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that inability to analyse a product's composition prior to filing does not automatically exclude it from prior art status.
